Take the lower-left corner of the grid as \((0,0)\). Let the endpoints of the horizontal segment be
\[
A=(1,1),\qquad B=(6,1),
\]
and the endpoints of the diagonal segment be
\[
C=(5,3),\qquad D=(8,7).
\]
Both segments have length \(5\).

A rotation must pair the endpoints in one of two ways.

### 1. \(A\to C\) and \(B\to D\)

If the center is \(O=(x,y)\), then \(OA=OC\) and \(OB=OD\):
\[
(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=(x-5)^2+(y-3)^2
\]
which simplifies to
\[
2x+y=8,
\]
and
\[
(x-6)^2+(y-1)^2=(x-8)^2+(y-7)^2
\]
which simplifies to
\[
x+3y=19.
\]
Solving gives
\[
(x,y)=(1,6),
\]
which is the marked point \(Z\).

Indeed, about \(Z\), the vectors
\[
\overrightarrow{ZA}=(0,-5),\quad \overrightarrow{ZC}=(4,-3)
\]
and
\[
\overrightarrow{ZB}=(5,-5),\quad \overrightarrow{ZD}=(7,1)
\]
have the same corresponding rotation.

### 2. \(A\to D\) and \(B\to C\)

The corresponding distance equations are
\[
14x+12y=111,\qquad 2x-4y=3,
\]
whose solution is
\[
(x,y)=\left(6,\frac94\right).
\]
This point is not marked; in particular, \(X=(6,2)\), not \((6,\frac94)\).

Therefore, the only marked point that could be the center is \(Z\).
